experiment: Rapture Reproducer V4 — Executable Incident Repair-Value Experiment
frozen_before: any candidate screening, any evidence-pack construction, any subject-agent run
question_class: product value, not mechanism. V0-V3.3 asked whether executable incidents can be produced safely and practically. V4 asks whether the artifact is actually worth anything.
product_thesis_under_test: A production bug that can be executed offline is materially easier for a coding agent to repair correctly than the same bug represented only by conventional telemetry and repository context.
kill_philosophy: If the executable incident does not materially improve repair outcomes against a STRONG control, kill the Reproducer product thesis even though the underlying systems engineering succeeded.

v3_3_freeze.verified: 20/20 checks; Phase 4 aggregates re-derived from raw artifacts; 0 drift across 14 files
v3_3_freeze.rule: capture, oracle, replay, ownership, privacy, selection, quiescence, reduction and unsupported-boundary implementations are FROZEN for all V4 headline cases
forbidden_changes: no product CLI or hosted service
v3_3_freeze.unsupported_case_rule: if a fresh historical bug falls outside the frozen V3.3 boundary, record it as unsupported. Do NOT change Rapture to make the case pass.

hypotheses.H1: treatment (conventional evidence + executable .repro) achieves a materially higher correct-fix rate than control (conventional evidence alone)
hypotheses.H2: among successful repairs, treatment reduces wall-clock time and repair iteration count
hypotheses.H3: treatment reduces false fixes because the agent has a direct executable oracle
hypotheses.H4: the advantage persists on fresh bugs never used in V0-V3.3
hypotheses.H5: the effect is not specific to one coding-agent runtime
hypotheses.H0: strong modern agents with conventional telemetry and repository access already repair these bugs about as well as agents with an executable incident

eligibility: public, pre-existing historical Node.js or TypeScript backend bug
no bug used in V0, V1, V2, V3, V3.1, V3.2 or V3.3
prefer real service/framework request paths over direct utility-function harnesses
at most 2 headline cases may be dependency bugs exercised through a real service stack
exact buggy revision AND independently known fixing revision
reproduces as a bounded HTTP-facing failure or equivalent request-scoped operation
candidates are NOT selected based on whether an agent is likely to solve them
screening_integrity: freeze candidate-pool.json before any subject-agent repair run
record every screened candidate and every exclusion with its reason
do not replace difficult supported cases after repair results are observed
subject agents never run during eligibility screening
the historical fixing revision is available ONLY to the evaluator and corpus-validation tooling
phase_1_fresh_corpus.headline_denominator: ALL frozen AUTO_CAPTURE_SUPPORTED cases, never a hand-picked subset

stage_1_gate.on_failure: stop before calibration and headline execution; report V4_CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT; do not broaden capture or replace difficult cases

phase_1_fresh_corpus.coverage_reporting: supported/unsupported yield is reported SEPARATELY from repair value; unsupported candidates are not hidden

per_bug: verify the buggy revision triggers the historical failure
verify the historical fixing revision removes it
build a hidden regression oracle distinguishing buggy from fixed behaviour
include multiple hidden variants exercising the same root cause with DIFFERENT concrete values where possible
run the repository's relevant regression suite
validate the oracle on BOTH revisions before any subject-agent run
freeze and hash all hidden evaluation material before headline runs
correct_fix_definition: the failure is not merely replaced by an unrelated infrastructure/setup failure
rules: alternative fixes are valid; similarity to the upstream patch is irrelevant and is NOT the oracle
the hidden oracle must never exist inside the subject-agent workspace
the fixing SHA, diff, commit message and future repository history must be inaccessible to subject agents

phase_3_control_evidence_pack.goal: represent competent modern observability, not a strawman
include: sanitized request shape and non-secret metadata
relevant application logs around the failure
trace-like span tree or ordered operation summary
database operation names/query text as normal observability would expose
database status/duration metadata but NOT captured result rows
outbound HTTP destination/operation/status/duration as normal observability would expose
release/revision identifier for the supplied buggy snapshot
exclude: upstream regression test added by the fix where it exposes the answer
manually supplied causal facts unavailable from normal incident telemetry
phase_3_control_evidence_pack.fairness_rule: CONTROL and TREATMENT receive BYTE-IDENTICAL conventional evidence packs. The only intended difference is the executable .repro available to TREATMENT.

phase_4_treatment_artifact.definition: the identical conventional evidence pack PLUS the frozen reduced executable incident
requirements: generated before any subject-agent run using the frozen V3.3 system
reproduces the exact original failure against the buggy revision
the historical fixed revision removes the original failure
offline replay verified with live DB/network disabled
contains no historical fix data, issue identifier or hidden evaluator data
hashed and frozen

experiment_only_runner.purpose: a stable way for the subject agent to execute the frozen artifact against its current worktree, without productizing a CLI
interface: one command to execute the incident against current code

requirements: fresh independent workspace per run, from the exact buggy source snapshot
upstream git remote removed
no future git history: a NEW single-commit repository containing only the buggy snapshot, so git log/show cannot reveal the fix
dependencies pre-provisioned before the run
no V4 evaluator files exposed
no other run's transcripts, patches or results exposed
fresh agent session per run
clean temporary HOME/config so agents inherit no unrelated global instructions or prior-run memory
repository-native AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md kept only if genuinely present at the buggy revision; both arms receive them identically
network_policy: no arbitrary web research about the historical bug
curl/wget/browser/package-search blocked or denied where the runtime permits
subject-agent traces scanned for attempted external lookup
any run obtaining the historical fix from the internet is INVALID_LEAKAGE and does not count

primary_runtime.selection_rule: before headline runs, select the strongest installed and authenticated coding-agent runtime invocable in isolated fresh sessions; prefer a runtime different from the orchestrating research agent where practical
primary_runtime.rule: model and effort level are IDENTICAL between CONTROL and TREATMENT

secondary_runtime.purpose: cross-runtime replication of a positive primary result
secondary_runtime.conditional: run ONLY if the primary satisfies STRONG_PRODUCT_SIGNAL; if the primary is KILL, do not spend runs attempting rescue
secondary_runtime.if_unavailable: record NOT_AVAILABLE rather than substituting another configuration of the same runtime after seeing results

control_core: You are repairing a production backend bug.
The supplied repository is the buggy production revision.
Use the supplied incident evidence and repository to identify and fix the bug.
You may inspect and modify application code and run available local tests.
Do not use the internet or search for the historical issue/fix.
Do not modify files outside the supplied repository.
Do not disable tests merely to obtain green output.
When you believe the bug is fixed, stop and provide a concise final report containing root cause, files changed, validation performed and remaining uncertainty.
treatment_addition_only: An executable incident artifact is available in the workspace.
You may run it using the supplied experiment-only repro command against the current working tree.
It reproduces the original production failure when that failure is present.
fairness: no other wording difference between arms
treatment is NOT told Rapture is being evaluated
control is NOT told another arm has an executable artifact
hidden evaluation criteria are not revealed beyond normal instruction to fix without regressions

phase_8_calibration.purpose: validate the harness, NOT estimate treatment effect
rules: use historical bugs PERMANENTLY excluded from the headline corpus
exercise both CONTROL and TREATMENT (4 runs total)
validate timeout behaviour, workspace sanitation, trace capture, evaluator isolation, artifact execution and final-result parsing
choose and freeze the per-run wall-clock budget BEFORE headline runs
do not tune prompts based on headline bugs
calibration outcomes are NEVER used in product-value estimates
phase_8_calibration.initial_budget: 20 minutes per repair run unless calibration demonstrates a clear infrastructure need for a different fixed budget, chosen before headline freeze

phase_9_headline.cases: ALL frozen AUTO_CAPTURE_SUPPORTED fresh bugs, minimum 8
phase_9_headline.concurrency_reason: wall-clock time is a measured outcome; concurrent runs would confound it with host/provider contention
randomization: generate and freeze a random seed before the first headline run
randomize arm order per bug and replicate
interleave arms rather than running all controls then all treatments
record the complete schedule before execution
fixed_budget: timeout is a legitimate outcome, not a reason to extend one arm
no_feedback: the hidden evaluator is never run interactively for the subject agent
the agent is never told why a hidden evaluation failed
each replicate is one independent attempt

procedure: run the hidden evaluator only after the agent terminates
phase_11_hidden_evaluation.false_fix_definition: the agent claims completion/success but hidden evaluation does not classify the patch CORRECT_FIX
phase_11_hidden_evaluation.primary_outcome: correct_fix_rate; agent self-report is NEVER sufficient

requirements: TREATMENT correct-fix rate improves by >= 15 absolute percentage points
treatment has a higher per-bug success rate on >= 60% of headline bugs
treatment has a lower per-bug success rate on <= 20% of headline bugs
treatment false-fix rate not worse by more than 5 percentage points
treatment regression rate not worse than control
treatment correct-fix rate not worse by more than 5 percentage points
median successful-run wall-clock time improves by >= 25% OR median repair-iteration count improves by >= 30%
at least one second efficiency metric improves by >= 20%
treatment false-fix and regression rates not worse

decision_rules.CONTINUE: primary runtime meets STRONG_PRODUCT_SIGNAL, no safety/integrity gate fails, and any available independent secondary runtime replicates directionally and non-harmfully. Proceed to minimal product/dogfood design. Do NOT reopen capture research.
decision_rules.KILL: treatment correct-fix improvement < 10 percentage points when control is below ceiling AND no >=20% meaningful efficiency improvement; OR treatment meaningfully worsens correctness, false fixes or regressions; OR agents rarely use the artifact and metrics show no material benefit; OR the advantage disappears against the strong conventional pack. Kill the product thesis rather than inventing V5 mechanism work.
decision_rules.MODIFY: ONLY for a narrow external-validity problem: severe control ceiling, insufficient supported fresh corpus, or subject-runtime infrastructure failure preventing an answer. NOT for a merely mediocre effect.
decision_rules.INVALID_EXPERIMENT: historical fix leaks; hidden evaluator becomes visible; arms receive materially different conventional evidence; frozen V3.3 capture modified for headline cases; prompts/budgets/model settings change after outcomes observed; headline bugs replaced based on repair difficulty; subject agents share outputs across replicates

anti_goalpost_rules: do not weaken the CONTROL to make .repro look useful
do not provide only a stack trace as the control
do not increase treatment time/token budget
do not give treatment extra root-cause prose
do not exclude bugs because CONTROL solves them too easily
do not exclude bugs because TREATMENT fails
do not tune .repro after a repair agent struggles
do not inspect the upstream fix while manually helping a subject run
do not give agents web access to search historical bug identifiers
do not add an agent-specific hint based on earlier replicates
do not convert a weak treatment effect into a new infrastructure experiment
do not introduce agent-procedure-conformance work into V4

stage_1_stop_point.rule: after corpus construction and the 4 calibration runs, STOP. No headline run begins without explicit approval.
